validity.recommendation: No existence, classification, or duplicate concern. Transwestern Pipeline Company, LLC is a real, currently-operating FERC-jurisdictional interstate natural-gas transmission mainline running from San Juan Basin/Permian Basin/Anadarko-area supply points in New Mexico and West Texas west to California, Arizona, and Nevada, with an eastbound intrastate-Texas/Midwest delivery capability as well. Confirmed independently and currently via: (1) Energy Transfer LP's FY2024 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2025), which lists Transwestern among its wholly-owned interstate gas pipeline assets with mileage/capacity figures; (2) Exhibit 21.1 of that same 10-K, naming the operating subsidiary 'Transwestern Pipeline Company, LLC'; (3) three separate-year Arizona Corporation Commission 'Summer Preparedness' filings (2016, 2018, 2019) by Transwestern itself to a state regulator; (4) a 2005 SEC Form 8-K/A exhibit (Transwestern's own audited financial statements, pre-ETP-acquisition, under prior owner CrossCountry Energy/Southern Union-GE JV); (5) a pipelinesafetyinfo.com New Mexico operator-disclosure PDF; (6) Wikipedia. Checked against the 46-row roster for a duplicate/relabel risk: no other roster row plausibly overlaps this system (no shared name, no shared FERC docket, no shared route found in any source read for this row) -- classification as 'transmission'/'operating' is corroborated by every source above and not contested by any.
validity.researcher_notes: Distinct from the real, currently-proposed 'Desert Southwest Expansion' project (Energy Transfer/Transwestern, ~516-520 mi new pipe, ~2029 target, ~$5.3B) found via the gem.wiki page and WebSearch -- this expansion has no corresponding ProjectID anywhere in the given 46-row roster, so it does not fit the cross_row_leads schema (which requires an existing roster PID) and is not staged as one; flagging it here and in the shard summary as a Discovery-candidate lead for the orchestrator instead.

validity.recommendation: Owner1='ETP Legacy' is a stale/miswritten placeholder, not a real current corporate entity. Energy Transfer Partners, L.P. (ETP) acquired 100% of Transwestern by December 1, 2006, but ETP itself was absorbed into Energy Transfer LP (formerly Energy Transfer Equity, L.P.) via the 2018 ETE/ETP 'simplification' merger -- 'ETP' has not existed as a standalone reporting entity since 2018. The current (FY2024 10-K, filed 2025) owner is Energy Transfer LP, 100%, operating through subsidiary Transwestern Pipeline Company, LLC.
validity.researcher_notes: Confirmed by 3 independent-in-origin sources: SEC Exhibit 21.1 (FY2024 10-K subsidiary list, naming Transwestern Pipeline Company, LLC as an ET subsidiary), the FY2024 10-K's own ownership table (Transwestern 100%), and Arizona Corporation Commission filings across 3 separate years (2016/2018/2019), each headed 'AN ENERGY TRANSFER COMPANY' and each showing Transwestern ('TW') at 100% ownership -- a state regulator filing, independent of the federal SEC filing per the source-independence rule. Wikipedia's current infobox also states owner='Energy Transfer', sourced independently of GEM.

validity.recommendation: Sheet Capacity=2835.00 MMcf/d is materially overstated versus every independent, dated, primary source found. Arizona Corporation Commission filings state Transwestern's capacity as 2.0 Bcf/d (2016) and 2.1 Bcf/d (2018 and 2019, each explicitly '~2.1 Bcf/d delivery capacity' in the system-overview text plus a matching 2.1 figure in the summary table); Energy Transfer LP's FY2024 10-K states exactly '2.1' Bcf/d in its asset table. All three independent, dated sources agree at 2.1 Bcf/d = 2100 MMcf/d as the current figure -- roughly 735 MMcf/d (26%) below the sheet's 2835.00.
validity.researcher_notes: 3 independent sources (AZCC 2018, AZCC 2019, ET FY2024 10-K) all agree on 2.1 Bcf/d current capacity; AZCC 2016 shows a slightly lower 2.0 Bcf/d (consistent with capacity growth over time via subsequent expansions, not a contradiction). No source found corroborates 2835 MMcf/d; could not determine where GEM's stored figure originated (not traceable to the 2017 Wikipedia citation GEM harvested for this row, which does not state a capacity figure at all).

validity.recommendation: Sheet LengthKnown=4345.00 km (2,700 mi) is likely overstated versus the cluster of independent, dated primary/regulatory sources found, which run 2,570-2,600 mi across 2016-2019 and land at exactly 2,590 mi in the most current source (Energy Transfer's FY2024 10-K asset table). A 2005 SEC 8-K/A (Transwestern's own pre-ETP audited financials) also describes a system of roughly 2,500 mi. This is a genuine but softer discrepancy than the Capacity finding: Energy Transfer's own marketing/PSA materials and the original 2017 Wikipedia citation GEM harvested for this row both independently state ~2,700 mi, so 'system mileage' appears to be reported inconsistently even across the company's own materials depending on measurement basis/vintage/what laterals are counted.
validity.researcher_notes: Candidate 4168.20 km = 2,590 mi (FY2024 10-K, the single most current and authoritative figure) x 1.609344. Corroborating cluster: AZCC 2016/2018 ('The system consists of approximately 2,600 miles of large diameter pipeline'), AZCC 2019 (2,570 in its summary table, but the same '~2,600 miles' system-overview prose repeated), 2005 SEC 8-K/A (~2,500 mi). Tier set to medium-leaning-high given the softer, self-inconsistent nature of the discrepancy (Energy Transfer's own 2,700-mi marketing figure is not simply wrong, likely a different, broader measurement basis) -- recommend a human check against a FERC tariff/system map before mechanically overwriting, rather than treating this as cleanly resolved.

validity.recommendation: EndState/Province='Texas-Oklahoma Panhandle, California, Arizona' mixes a supply-basin descriptor into what should be an end-market/delivery-state list, and omits Nevada, a confirmed served market. Wikipedia's own prose places 'the Texas-Oklahoma Panhandle' alongside 'southwest Colorado' and 'the Permian Basin' as ORIGIN/supply regions (not destinations). Energy Transfer's FY2024 10-K states the system 'access[es] Texas and Midcontinent natural gas market hubs as well as major western markets in Arizona, Nevada and California' -- naming Nevada explicitly, and a pipelinesafetyinfo.com New Mexico disclosure independently states the system 'traverses to markets in the Midwest, Texas, Arizona, New Mexico, Nevada and California.'
validity.researcher_notes: Tempering caveat, not fully resolved: the system is genuinely bidirectional -- a 2005 SEC 8-K/A states Transwestern also 'delivers natural gas from the east end of its system to Texas intrastate and Midwest markets,' so Texas/Midwest end-delivery is real too, just mischaracterized on the sheet as a supply-basin name ('Texas-Oklahoma Panhandle') rather than as an actual eastbound end market. Recommend a human judgment call on how to represent a bidirectional system in a single-direction EndState/Province field rather than a mechanical replace; the clean, unambiguous part of this finding is that Nevada is missing and 'Texas-Oklahoma Panhandle' is not itself an end-market name.
